title: Corn/Soybeans/Wheat - Which Chart Looks BULLISH?? - with Brian Splitt

bullets: Jan27 beans fell ~12c to $12.19; Dec26 corn fell ~6c to ~$4.42. Drivers: firmer USD and good South America weather
Wheat had double-digit losses despite Black Sea worries. Grains bounced overnight
Most bullish chart: soybeans, the only one of the three still in an uptrend since January
Jan beans: move high $12.36, retaken overnight, and back above the 20-day MA
Corn: capped at the 20-day MA. Support ~$4.40, then the Aug low ~$4.34 and the trendline ~$4.10–4.12
Corn spreads firmed even on down days (Dec/Mar narrowest since about early April), which he reads as a bottoming signal
Wheat: HRW down 10 straight weeks. Key level ~$5.68
USDA raised US bean exports more than production, so carryout fell; the focus shifts to Brazil
El Niño is making southern Brazil too wet. Private Brazil soy estimates go as low as the low 170s MMT
BRL futures are down ~12% since the election, and beans have decoupled from the weak real
Flash sale: 136k mt of beans to China. Total soy sales are running 76% ahead of last year
China is at ~65.4% of the 25 MMT target. The $17B non-soy ag pledge is lagging (~$7B done)
Ethanol output 1.13M bpd, a seasonal record. Stocks 24.35M bbl. Margins +35–50c/gal
CTVA fell ~24%, a record one-day drop, with Brazil sales down 31%. The read-through is a risk to Brazil yields
Drought covers 29% of the Corn Belt, and 48% of winter wheat areas
Little drought in Kansas plus high insurance guarantees means big winter wheat acreage, which is bearish for wheat
Live cattle up as much as 2.43, feeders up 3.05–4.18
Splitt is eyeing short-term puts near $226.50–227 in Feb live cattle
No Fed or rates talk beyond a firmer USD and high Brazilian interest rates

flags: The HRW insurance guarantee was heard as “811” (probably ~$8.11)
